name: South Asia
blurb: Music, cinema, history, food and geography from India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Nepal, Bhutan, the Maldives and Afghanistan.

clues.q: This Chennai-born composer won two Academy Awards for his work on the 2008 film “Slumdog Millionaire.”
This Pakistani TV music series, first aired in 2008, is known for live fusion performances such as the 2022 viral hit “Pasoori.”
Which instrument is Ravi Shankar most famous for playing?
Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan brought this devotional Sufi singing tradition to audiences around the world.
This legendary playback singer, who sang “Ae Mere Watan Ke Logon,” received the Bharat Ratna in 2001 and died in 2022.
In this 2001 Aamir Khan film, villagers take on British officers in a cricket match to escape a heavy tax.
This 1995 Shah Rukh Khan–Kajol romance, known by the initials “DDLJ,” ran for decades at Mumbai’s Maratha Mandir theater.
clues.a: What is Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge?

clues.q: This Bengali filmmaker directed “Pather Panchali” (1955) and received an honorary Academy Award in 1992.
This 2022 Telugu film by S. S. Rajamouli won the Academy Award for Best Original Song for “Naatu Naatu.”
This 1960 epic directed by K. Asif stars Dilip Kumar as Prince Salim and Madhubala as Anarkali.
This Bronze Age civilization included the planned cities of Harappa and Lothal.
clues.a: What is the Indus Valley Civilization?

clues.q: This Mauryan emperor embraced Buddhism after the devastating Kalinga War.
Siddhartha Gautama, the founder of Buddhism, was born at this site in present-day Nepal.
The oldest of the four Vedas, this collection of more than 1,000 hymns honors deities such as Agni and Indra.
Ruled by Chandragupta I and Samudragupta, this dynasty presided over what is often called a classical “Golden Age” of India.
India and Pakistan both gained independence from British rule in this year.
In 1971, the region formerly known as East Pakistan became this independent country.
In 1960, this Ceylonese politician became the world’s first female prime minister.
In 1984, this Indian Air Force pilot became the first Indian citizen in space, flying aboard a Soviet Soyuz mission.
In 2014, this Pakistani education activist became the youngest person ever awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
This yogurt-based drink, served sweet or salty, is a favorite across India and Pakistan.
These bowl-shaped Sri Lankan pancakes are made from fermented rice flour and coconut milk, sometimes with an egg cooked in the middle.
This layered rice-and-meat dish has famous regional styles from Hyderabad, Lucknow and Karachi.
These steamed or fried dumplings are a beloved street food in Nepal.
Made of chilies cooked in cheese, this spicy stew is considered Bhutan’s national dish.
The highest mountain on Earth sits on the border of Nepal and China.
This Indian Ocean nation is made up of roughly 1,200 coral islands grouped into atolls.
This sacred river flows past the city of Varanasi on its way to the Bay of Bengal.
This historic mountain pass connects Afghanistan and Pakistan through the Spin Ghar range.
Shared by India and Bangladesh, this vast mangrove forest is a UNESCO World Heritage site famous for its tigers.
This pair of hand drums is the main percussion instrument of Hindustani classical music.
This singer shot to fame with “Tum Hi Ho” from the 2013 film “Aashiqui 2.”
Yaman and Bhairavi are examples of this melodic framework at the heart of Indian classical music.
Associated with the poet Ghalib and singers like Mehdi Hassan and Jagjit Singh, this poetic song form often explores love and longing.
This Pakistani pop band released the patriotic anthem “Dil Dil Pakistan” in 1987.
The nickname of Mumbai’s Hindi film industry blends the city’s old name with “Hollywood.”
This 2009 Aamir Khan comedy about three engineering students popularized the catchphrase “All is well.”
Who directed the 1957 classic “Mother India”?
Adapted from Farhat Ishtiaq’s novel, this 2011 Hum TV drama serial starred Fawad Khan and Mahira Khan as Ashar and Khirad.
Known to fans as “Thalaivar,” this Tamil superstar played both scientist and robot in “Enthiran” (2010).
Mahavira was the 24th Tirthankara of this ancient Indian religion.
Advised by the strategist Chanakya, this ruler founded the Maurya Empire.
This ancient Buddhist center of learning in Bihar attracted students from across Asia.
This ancient Sri Lankan capital is home to the sacred Sri Maha Bodhi tree.
In 326 BCE, this Macedonian king fought King Porus at the Battle of the Hydaspes.
Known as “Quaid-e-Azam,” this founder of Pakistan became its first Governor-General in 1947.
In 1947, this statesman became India’s first prime minister.
In 1953, Tenzing Norgay and this New Zealander became the first climbers confirmed to reach the summit of Everest.
This Bangladeshi economist and the Grameen Bank he founded shared the 2006 Nobel Peace Prize.
In 2008, this Himalayan kingdom adopted its first written constitution and became a constitutional monarchy with an elected National Assembly.
This “festival of lights” celebrates the victory of light over darkness with lamps called diyas.
This spring festival is celebrated by throwing colored powder and water.
Celebrated in Bangladesh on April 14 with greetings of “Shubho Noboborsho,” this festival marks the first day of the Bengali calendar year.
Marking the end of Ramadan, this Muslim festival is often called “Meethi Eid” for sweets like sheer khurma.
Held each year in Kandy, Sri Lanka, this grand procession of decorated elephants honors the Sacred Tooth Relic of the Buddha.
Nicknamed the “Little Master,” this Indian batsman became the first cricketer to score 100 international centuries, in 2012.
In this South Asian contact sport, a “raider” must tag opponents and return to their half while holding their breath.
This Sri Lankan off-spinner retired from Test cricket in 2010 with exactly 800 wickets.
This Indian javelin thrower won Olympic gold at the Tokyo Games, held in 2021.
Pakistan won its first Cricket World Cup in this year, beating England in the final in Melbourne.

questions.q: Ancient Indian board game seen as chess’s ancestor?
Fried milk balls soaked in sugar syrup?
Long draped garment worn by women across South Asia?

clues.q: This Pakistani singer, nephew of Nusrat Fateh Ali Khan, sang “Teri Meri” for the 2011 film “Bodyguard.”
clues.a: Who is Rahat Fateh Ali Khan?
clues.hint: He shares much of his famous uncle’s name.

clues.q: Ustad Bismillah Khan was the great master of this oboe-like wind instrument, often heard at weddings.
clues.hint: A double-reed instrument with a flared bell.

clues.q: Indian classical music has two main traditions: Hindustani in the north and this one in the south.
clues.hint: Its name is linked to the region of Karnataka.

clues.q: Which lively Sri Lankan song-and-dance style has roots in Portuguese colonial-era music?
clues.hint: Its name comes from the Portuguese verb “bailar,” to dance.

clues.q: This Bengali song tradition comprises more than 2,000 songs written and composed by Rabindranath Tagore.
clues.hint: It is named after its creator; the second word means “music.”

clues.q: This 2016 Aamir Khan film tells the story of wrestler Mahavir Singh Phogat and his daughters.
clues.hint: Its one-word title means “wrestling competition.”

clues.q: Pakistan’s film industry is nicknamed “Lollywood” after this city.
clues.hint: Capital of Punjab province.

clues.q: This 2015 S. S. Rajamouli epic ended on a cliffhanger about why Kattappa killed its title hero.
clues.hint: Its sequel was subtitled “The Conclusion.”

clues.q: This 2001 Mira Nair film about a chaotic Punjabi family wedding in Delhi won the Golden Lion at Venice.
clues.hint: The title pairs a rainy season with a celebration.

clues.q: Directed by Tareque Masud, this 2002 film became Bangladesh’s first-ever submission for the Academy Award for Best Foreign Language Film.
clues.hint: Its English title is “The Clay Bird.”

clues.q: Attributed to the sage Valmiki, this Sanskrit epic tells of Prince Rama’s exile and the rescue of Sita.
clues.hint: Its name means “Rama’s journey.”

clues.q: This ancient Sanskrit treatise on statecraft and economics is traditionally attributed to Kautilya.
clues.hint: Its name begins with the Sanskrit word for wealth.

clues.q: This ancient region in present-day northwest Pakistan and eastern Afghanistan lent its name to a Greco-Buddhist art style.
clues.hint: Peshawar and Taxila lay within it.

clues.q: The Chinese pilgrim Faxian traveled through India during the reign of this Gupta emperor, also called Vikramaditya.
clues.hint: Son of Samudragupta.

clues.q: Famous for their Buddhist murals, these rock-cut caves in Maharashtra date from about the 2nd century BCE to the 5th century CE.
clues.hint: Not Ellora, but their famous neighbor.

clues.q: In 1966, this daughter of Jawaharlal Nehru became India’s first female prime minister.
clues.hint: Her married surname is very famous in India.

clues.q: In 1988, this politician became the first woman to serve as Pakistan’s prime minister.
clues.hint: Her father had also led Pakistan.

clues.q: Founded in Dhaka in 1985, this regional body brought together South Asian nations for cooperation.
clues.hint: A five-letter acronym for a regional association.

clues.q: In 1991, this Indian finance minister, who later became prime minister, launched sweeping economic liberalization reforms.
clues.hint: An Oxford- and Cambridge-trained economist in a blue turban.

clues.q: In August 2023, this Indian lunar mission became the first to soft-land near the Moon’s south pole.
clues.hint: Its name means “moon craft” plus a number.

clues.q: This is the official language of Bangladesh, also widely spoken in West Bengal.
clues.hint: Speakers call it “Bangla.”

clues.q: This script is used to write Hindi, Marathi and Nepali.
clues.hint: Letters hang from a horizontal top line.

clues.q: Along with Sinhala, this is one of Sri Lanka’s two official languages.
clues.hint: Also the official language of Tamil Nadu.

clues.q: Written in the right-to-left Thaana script, this is the official language of the Maldives.
clues.hint: Closely related to Sinhala.

clues.q: Under Afghanistan’s 2004 constitution, the two official languages were Pashto and this variety of Persian.
clues.hint: A four-letter name.

clues.q: This white-marble mausoleum in Agra was commissioned by Mughal emperor Shah Jahan in memory of his wife.
clues.hint: It stands on the bank of the Yamuna River.

clues.q: Completed under Aurangzeb in 1673, this red-sandstone mosque faces Lahore Fort.
clues.hint: Its name means “the emperor’s” mosque.

clues.q: This 5th-century rock fortress in Sri Lanka is famed for its frescoes and its Lion Gate.
clues.hint: Often called “Lion Rock.”

clues.q: Built around a cave where Guru Rinpoche is said to have meditated, this Buddhist monastery clings to a cliff above Bhutan’s Paro Valley.
clues.a: What is the Tiger’s Nest (Paro Taktsang)?
clues.hint: Named after a big cat’s home.

clues.q: Nicknamed the “Monkey Temple,” this hilltop stupa in Kathmandu has the Buddha’s eyes painted on its tower.
clues.hint: Its name means “self-existent” or “self-arisen.”

clues.q: Driven by the dhol drum, this energetic Punjabi folk music and dance style is now a staple at parties worldwide.
clues.hint: Think harvest celebrations in Punjab.

clues.q: This tabla maestro, son of Alla Rakha, won multiple Grammy Awards and played with the fusion band Shakti.
clues.hint: Often addressed with the title “Ustad.”

clues.q: Honored with the title “Malika-e-Tarannum” (Queen of Melody), this singer-actress moved to Pakistan after 1947.
clues.hint: Her name means “light of the world.”

clues.q: The shrine of Lal Shahbaz Qalandar, celebrated in the qawwali “Dama Dam Mast Qalandar,” is located in which country?
clues.hint: The shrine stands in the town of Sehwan Sharif.

clues.q: Today the predominant genre of Hindustani classical vocal music, this form takes its name from an Arabic-Persian word often translated as “imagination.”
clues.hint: Not dhrupad, its older and more austere cousin.

clues.q: In this 2023 action film, Shah Rukh Khan plays a spy known by a single codename that gives the film its title.
clues.hint: Part of the YRF Spy Universe.

clues.q: Directed by B. R. Chopra, this TV adaptation of a Sanskrit epic aired on Doordarshan from 1988 to 1990.
clues.hint: The epic includes the Bhagavad Gita.

clues.q: This 1975 Hindi blockbuster starring Amitabh Bachchan and Dharmendra features the villain Gabbar Singh.
clues.hint: Its title means “embers.”

clues.q: Often called the father of Sinhala cinema, this director made “Rekava” in 1956.
clues.hint: A three-part name; he also directed “Gamperaliya.”

clues.q: Satyajit Ray’s “Apu Trilogy” consists of “Pather Panchali,” “Aparajito” and this 1959 film.
clues.hint: In English: “The World of Apu.”

clues.q: The Vedas were composed in an early form of this classical language.
clues.hint: Its name means “refined” or “perfected.”

clues.q: First commissioned by Ashoka, this great stupa in Madhya Pradesh is famous for its carved gateways.
clues.hint: Its name rhymes with “Ranchi.”

clues.q: Used for most of Ashoka’s edicts, this ancient script is the ancestor of most modern South Asian scripts.
clues.hint: Shares a root with the name of a Hindu creator god.

clues.q: A major patron of Buddhism, this Kushan emperor ruled from Purushapura, modern Peshawar, around the 2nd century CE.
clues.hint: The Kushan era’s most famous ruler.

clues.q: This Neolithic site in Balochistan, Pakistan, is one of the earliest known farming settlements in South Asia.
clues.hint: It predates the Indus Valley cities by millennia.

clues.q: In 1948, this island, then called Ceylon, gained independence from Britain.
clues.hint: Its largest city is Colombo.

clues.q: Nicknamed the “Missile Man,” this aerospace scientist served as India’s president from 2002 to 2007.
clues.a: Who is A. P. J. Abdul Kalam?
clues.hint: Known as “the People’s President.”

clues.q: India’s national space agency was founded in 1969 and is known by this four-letter acronym.
clues.hint: The R stands for “Research.”

clues.q: In 1979, this Pakistani physicist shared the Nobel Prize in Physics for work on electroweak unification.
clues.hint: He shared it with Glashow and Weinberg.

clues.q: Bhutan’s Fourth King championed this development philosophy in the 1970s, valuing well-being over GDP.
clues.hint: A cheerful twist on “Gross National Product.”

clues.q: In 1913, this Bengali poet of “Gitanjali” became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.
clues.hint: Often called “Gurudev.”

clues.q: Born Mirza Asadullah Baig Khan, this 19th-century Delhi poet is among the most celebrated writers of Urdu ghazals.
clues.hint: Known by his pen name.

clues.q: Called the “Poet of the East,” this poet-philosopher wrote the verses of “Saare Jahan Se Achha.”
clues.hint: Pakistan’s national poet.

clues.q: Set in Kerala, this debut novel by Arundhati Roy won the 1997 Booker Prize.
clues.a: What is The God of Small Things?
clues.hint: Its central characters are the twins Estha and Rahel.

clues.q: This Colombo-born Canadian author won the 1992 Booker Prize for “The English Patient.”
clues.hint: His memoir is “Running in the Family.”

clues.q: This big cat is the national animal of both India and Bangladesh.
clues.hint: Named after a region of the subcontinent.

clues.q: Nepal’s Chitwan National Park and India’s Kaziranga are strongholds of this armored, single-horned mammal.
clues.hint: Also called the greater one-horned species.

clues.q: Pakistan’s national animal is this wild goat with spectacular corkscrew horns.
clues.hint: Its Persian name is usually translated “snake-eater,” from a folk belief that it kills snakes.

clues.q: Known locally as the danphe, this iridescent pheasant is Nepal’s national bird.
clues.hint: It is also the state bird of Uttarakhand.

clues.q: Bhutan’s national animal is this sturdy goat-antelope of the eastern Himalayas.
clues.hint: Five letters; it looks like a cross between a moose and a goat.

questions.q: Which country has the world’s only non-rectangular national flag?
Most of the Hindu Kush mountain range lies in which country?
Ceylon’s coffee plantations were largely replaced in the late 1800s by which crop, now its most famous export?
What is the English name of the chain of shoals between India and Sri Lanka, also called Ram Setu?
Which ruler founded the Mughal Empire after the First Battle of Panipat in 1526?
Which Indian city is popularly nicknamed the “City of Joy”?
Jaipur is popularly known by which nickname?
The Sri Lankan street food kottu is mainly made from what?
Which Mughal emperor’s Delhi tomb is a UNESCO site often seen as a forerunner of the Taj Mahal?
Which narrow sea channel separates India’s Tamil Nadu from northern Sri Lanka?

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: Excavated beginning in the 1920s and now a UNESCO World Heritage site in Pakistan’s Sindh province, this Bronze Age city is famous for its Great Bath and the bronze “Dancing Girl” statuette.
rounds.hint: Its name is often translated as “Mound of the Dead.”

rounds.name: Final Round
rounds.q: A UNESCO World Heritage site in Bihar, this town’s Mahabodhi Temple marks the place where Siddhartha Gautama is said to have attained enlightenment beneath a fig tree.
